sourceName: Cracker Barrel store locations near the I-5 Central Valley corridor (Bakersfield to Sacramento) -- AllStays directory cross-checked against Cracker Barrel Careers job postings and news coverage
method: Task scope: find NEW Cracker Barrel locations near the mile-100-to-400 I-5 Central Valley gap (Bakersfield area -> Coalinga -> Los Banos -> Patterson -> Tracy/Lathrop -> Stockton -> Elk Grove/Sacramento) that are not already in public/data/sleep-cracker-barrel.geojson. Confirmed via the AllStays CA directory (cross-checked against Cracker Barrel's own careers.crackerbarrel.com job listings, which independently confirm store cities) that California has exactly 5 Cracker Barrel locations total: Camarillo, Rialto, Rocklin, Victorville, and Bakersfield. Camarillo, Rocklin, and Victorville are already recorded in the existing dataset (scripts/sources/crackerbarrel-locations.json / public/data/sleep-cracker-barrel.geojson) and were not re-added here. Rialto (1080 W. Renaissance Pkwy, Rialto CA) sits on I-10/CA-210 and was already evaluated and excluded as off-corridor by the existing source file's method note -- confirmed still true, not on this trip's I-5/US-50/I-80 corridors, not re-added. Bakersfield (3310 California Ave, Bakersfield, CA 93304) was newly researched for this task: address corroborated across TruRating, DoorDash, Tripadvisor, and Cracker Barrel's own Bakersfield careers postings, and geocoded via OpenStreetMap Nominatim to 35.3687,-119.0396. That store sits in the city of Bakersfield on CA-99/local streets. The trip's actual I-5 alignment splits from CA-99 at the Wheeler Ridge interchange (I-5/SR-99 junction, ~35.00,-119.03 -- this is what the mile-101 route anchor at 35.1212,-119.0658 corresponds to) and continues northwest through Lost Hills/Kettleman City/Coalinga, bypassing Bakersfield entirely. Driving distance from Wheeler Ridge into Bakersfield via SR-99 is documented (AARoads CA-99 guide) as 27 miles each way -- far beyond the ~10-driving-mile corridor threshold for this task. Excluded on distance grounds; this is a real, existing Cracker Barrel, just not usable for this route.
policyNote: No change from the existing dataset's finding: Cracker Barrel corporate has stated (per a May 6, 2025 TheTravel.com article quoting the company directly) that overnight RV/car parking is a store-by-store manager decision based on local ordinances and lot layout, with no chain-wide guarantee -- see scripts/sources/crackerbarrel-locations.json for the original citation. Nothing new to add here since no new stores qualified.
